predecessors.name: West Francia
predecessors.text: 'the area of present-day Upper Normandy which Rollo had previously conquered', ceded by Charles the Simple under the Treaty of Saint-Clair-sur-Epte

successors.name: Norman England
successors.text: continental Normandy, which Cliopatria folds into its Norman England row from 1072 (that row's shape reaches lat 47.99 in France)

ledger.x: 911: the Treaty of Saint-Clair-sur-Epte gives Rollo the lower Seine.
933: William Longsword is granted the Cotentin and the Avranchin.
942: Louis IV takes the duchy after Longsword's murder (bridging a silence).
946: Louis IV is captured and Normandy is returned.
1071: the duchy passes into Norman England.

wars.name: Norman conquest of England
wars.outcome: Norman victory at Hastings on 14 October 1066, William crowned 25 December 1066, and the last English resistance ended at Ely in early 1071; the Treaty of Abernethy followed in 1072.

wars.name: Louis IV's war with Richard I of Normandy
wars.outcome: Louis IV seized the duchy, gave lower Normandy to Hugh the Great, was captured in 946 and recognised Richard as duke; Otto, Arnulf and Louis were driven from Rouen's gates in 947.

wars.name: Norman siege of Alençon and Domfront
wars.outcome: Alençon and Domfront surrendered to William; the History page has Passais taken in 1050.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a surveyed or treaty frontier for Normandy (the 911 treaty gives 'the area of present-day Upper Normandy'); the marches with Maine and Brittany shift by county.
